toc.title: Know the Boundary: When to Escalate

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. HR: human resources

  • How Claude supports design, build and iteration of a solution
  • How to fit Claude into an existing workflow: augment a step or redesign the flow
  • Patterns that work: draft and review, triage, extract, summarize
  • When to escalate to Developers or Architects
  • How to communicate value and limits honestly to stakeholders

2Supporting Solution Design and Iteration

Running case

Cedarbrook's Onboarding Kit

  • HR wants a new-hire onboarding kit: checklist, welcome email series, an FAQ and a short interactive quiz
  • The HR lead uses Claude to draft the structure, build an artifact quiz, test it with sample answers, and revise after feedback from two managers
Phase How Claude helps Your role
Design Options with trade-offs, outlines, mock-ups, process diagrams, templates Choose, adapt to your context
Build Draft documents, forms, spreadsheets with formulas, slide decks, simple interactive artifacts Review, test, own the result
Test Sample inputs, edge cases, checklists, "what could go wrong" lists Run the tests; judge the outcomes
Iterate Revise from feedback; compare versions; track changes in a summary Collect real user feedback
Document Instructions, FAQs, handover notes Confirm accuracy
  • Prototype fast, validate with users. A quick artifact or draft is a conversation starter, not a finished product.
  • Small, simple solutions (templates, checklists, spreadsheets, Projects, simple artifacts) are the Associate's territory.
  • For anything that needs code in production, API calls, databases or system integration, escalate (section 4).

3Fitting Claude into a Workflow

Approach What changes Example Risk
Augment One step gets faster or better; the process stays Agents get draft replies from Claude and send after review Low
Redesign Steps are removed, merged or reordered Instead of 5 hand-offs, Claude triages and drafts, a person approves once Higher: needs a pilot and clear ownership

Workflow patterns that work:

Pattern Flow
Draft and review Claude drafts; a person edits and approves
Triage and route Claude classifies and tags; a person handles the exceptions
Extract and structure Claude pulls fields from documents; a person spot-checks
Summarize and decide Claude summarizes long inputs; a person decides
Research and brief Claude gathers and cites; a person verifies and concludes

Building blocks inside Claude: Projects (standing instructions and knowledge), Skills (repeatable methods), connectors (Google Drive, Gmail, Slack and others), artifacts (shareable outputs), memory (continuity) (Modules 11 and 12).

Make it stick:

  • Name an owner for the prompt, the Project and the quality of the results
  • Write down when to use Claude and when not to
  • Keep review steps where errors matter
  • Share the prompts and Projects so everyone gets consistent results
  • Train the team (examples, do's and don'ts, how to verify)
  • Track KPIs (time saved, error rate, satisfaction) and review them
Exam tip

The safe answer for integration: start with augmentation and a human review, pilot, measure, then redesign where evidence supports it.

4Know the Boundary: When to Escalate

An Associate handles Escalate to a Developer or Architect
Prompts, Projects, instructions, knowledge Building against the API, code that calls Claude
Skills, artifacts, connectors from the directory Agents, automated multi-step pipelines, scheduled jobs at scale
Reviewing outputs and workflows Integrations with core systems and databases
Pilots and measures Security architecture, access control, data-residency design
Policy-compliant daily use Enterprise-scale deployment design and evaluation frameworks
  • The exam guide says plainly that Associates recognize limitations and escalate more complex or technical work.
  • Escalate when the solution needs custom code, automation without a human, large data volumes, or security and compliance design.
  • Bring a clear brief: the business goal, the current process, the data involved, volumes, risks and success measures.

5Communicating Value and Limits

Stakeholders need an honest picture: neither hype nor fear.

Say about value Say about limits
Time saved on drafting, summarizing, analysis (use pilot numbers) Claude can be wrong or invent details; outputs are reviewed
Consistency of tone and format with Projects and Skills It has a knowledge cutoff and only the tools and data you connect
Faster first drafts, so people spend time on judgment Sensitive data rules apply; not every task is allowed
Scale: handles volume spikes Bias can appear; people decisions need human oversight
Learning curve is short for common tasks Usage limits and costs exist; effort and model choices matter
  • Tailor the message: executives want outcomes, risk and cost; managers want workload and quality; staff want how it changes their job and what stays human; compliance wants data handling and review.
  • Back claims with evidence from a pilot, not vendor promises: "In the pilot, reply drafting time fell from 6 to 2 minutes; 4% of drafts needed corrections of facts."
  • Never promise that Claude is always accurate, replaces staff review, or can do things it is not connected to do.
  • Be open about what is still unknown and how you will learn it.
  • Show how people stay accountable: who reviews, who approves, who owns the policy.
Exam tip

The best stakeholder message is balanced, evidence-based and specific: real benefits, real limits, a review plan and a next step.

Exam tip

Pilot, measure, then scale: evidence from a small trial beats a promise, and any step Claude cannot do alone is a job for a Developer.

6Exam Q&A

S1Customer care agents currently write every reply from scratch. What is the lowest-risk way to bring Claude into this workflow?

  • ARemove the review step and send Claude's replies automatically
  • BBan Claude
  • CLet Claude draft replies that agents review and send
  • DReplace the agents
Show the answer

Answer: C. Augmenting with a draft-and-review step is low risk and quick to pilot.

S2A manager wants Claude connected directly to the order database through custom code, with scheduled automatic updates. What should the Associate do?

  • AIgnore the request
  • BEscalate to a Claude Developer or Architect with a clear brief
  • CBuild it themselves
  • DAsk Claude to write the code and run it unreviewed in production
Show the answer

Answer: B. API integration and automation at scale belong to Developers and Architects.

S3Which message to the leadership team is best?

  • A"We do not know anything yet."
  • B"In our pilot, drafting time fell by two thirds; about 4% of drafts needed fact fixes, so we keep a review step."
  • C"Claude is always accurate and will soon replace the review process, so reviewers can be moved to other work."
  • D"Claude cannot be trusted."
Show the answer

Answer: B. Specific evidence plus an honest limit and a control.

S4What is the main difference between augmenting and redesigning a workflow?

  • ARedesigning never needs a pilot
  • BAugmenting improves a step inside the current process; redesigning removes, merges or reorders steps
  • CAugmenting changes the whole process from the first day; redesigning changes only a single step in it
  • DThere is no difference
Show the answer

Answer: B. Augmentation keeps the process; redesign reshapes it and needs more care.

S5An HR lead builds a quiz artifact with Claude. What is the right next step?

  • ATest it with sample answers and real users, and revise from feedback
  • BDelete the testing steps because they slow the prototype down and add little value
  • CPublish it company-wide immediately so that everyone can start using it this week
  • DAssume it works
Show the answer

Answer: A. A prototype is a conversation starter, so it is tested with sample answers and real users and revised before wider use.

S6Which TWO are good practices when rolling Claude into a team workflow? Select TWO.

  • AKeep review steps where errors matter
  • BGive everyone a different private prompt style
  • CHide limits from staff
  • DAvoid tracking results
  • EName an owner for the prompts, the Project and the quality
Show the answer

Answer: A, E. Naming an owner and keeping review steps where errors matter keep quality accountable as more people start using Claude.

S7Which statement about talking to compliance stakeholders is best?

  • AAvoid mentioning data handling because it will only worry the compliance team unnecessarily
  • BExplain what data goes into Claude, which policy applies, and who reviews outputs
  • CPromise that decisions will be made automatically so that compliance has nothing left to review
  • DSay Claude never makes mistakes
Show the answer

Answer: B. Compliance wants to know what data enters Claude, which policy applies and who reviews outputs, not a promise of perfection.

S8Which workflow is a good "triage and route" example?

  • AClaude tags incoming support tickets by topic and urgency, and people handle the exceptions
  • BClaude approves every refund request on its own and informs the customer by email without any review
  • CClaude chooses suppliers alone
  • DClaude signs contracts
Show the answer

Answer: A. Classification with human exception handling is a safe and valuable pattern.

S9A team cannot tell whether Claude helps. What should they do?

  • AChoose KPIs (time, error rate, satisfaction), run a pilot and compare with the baseline
  • BAsk Claude to say yes, because Claude is the best judge of whether Claude has helped anybody
  • CGuess
  • DStop measuring
Show the answer

Answer: A. Only measured evidence from a pilot compared with a baseline can show whether Claude actually helps, rather than opinions or guesses.

S10Which request should an Associate escalate?

  • AImprove a prompt for meeting notes so that it produces cleaner action lists every time
  • BDesign secure access between Claude and several internal systems
  • CBuild a Project with brand instructions
  • DCreate a checklist
Show the answer

Answer: B. Secure integration across several internal systems with access controls is architecture work for a Developer or Architect, not an Associate task.

S11What belongs in a good brief when escalating to a Developer?

  • ANothing at all; the developers already know the whole context and the history of the process
  • BOnly "make it work"
  • CA request to guess the budget
  • DThe business goal, current process, data involved, volumes, risks and success measures
Show the answer

Answer: D. A clear brief lets the technical team design the right solution.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Design and iterate Claude drafts options, prototypes, tests; you validate with users
Augment vs redesign Augment a step (low risk) · redesign the flow (pilot first)
Patterns Draft and review · triage and route · extract and structure · summarize and decide · research and brief
Make it stick Owner · when-to-use rules · reviews · shared Projects · training · KPIs
Escalate API integration, agents, automation at scale, systems integration, security architecture
Brief Goal · process · data · volumes · risks · measures
Message Evidence-based value + plain limits + review plan + next step
Never promise Perfect accuracy; replacing review; connections that do not exist
